solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jersey-carrying possibly affected half-wit catching cold

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
affected in the sense of put on or contorted, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A pretentious fool has picked up a chill while wearing a woollen jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges HALFWIT into WITHALF; 'catching' puts C inside it. Jersey here is the breed of dairy cow from the Channel Island, not a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant cow is said to be carrying young, and a Jersey cow would be one example of such an expectant animal.

clue.text: Small boy tethers dogs

parts.note: Wes is a short form of the boy's name Wesley
to tether is to tie

explanation.surface: A little lad ties up the dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: These are West Highland white terriers, a breed of small dogs.

clue.text: Where to stand round at breakfast?

definitions.text: Where to stand round at breakfast?

parts.words: Where to stand round at breakfast?
parts.note: a round is a slice of toast, and a rack holds such slices upright on the breakfast table

explanation.walkthrough: 'stand round' suggests people standing about; here a round of toast is what stands.
explanation.definitionFit: This rack keeps cooked bread slices upright on the table at the morning meal.

clue.text: Rotating machine showing effect of sun after eclipses

indicators.note: after places the sun's effect behind the eclipsing word, though the clue names it first

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or eclipse
a tan is the browning of skin by sunshine

explanation.surface: A spinning device reveals how the sun looks after an eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum used for winding ropes, a rotating machine on ships.

clue.text: With pride, she and I performing in reduced circumstances

indicators.note: in says the I and performing go within the reduced letters

parts.note: less means reduced or smaller in amount
on means performing, on stage

explanation.surface: A proud woman and I put on a show although we are hard up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With pride' looks like an emotion; a pride is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the big cat, who lives with a group called a pride.

clue.text: Avoiding blame when our language teaching gets no backing

parts.note: TEFL is Teaching English as a Foreign Language, our language being English

indicators.note: backing means the little word no is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A school escapes criticism even though its English teaching lacks support.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician to whom nothing sticks, like a non-stick pan coating, is described with this trade name as an adjective.

clue.text: What was a woolly bear's extraordinary girth to me!

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at the size of a woolly bear's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: A woolly bear is the hairy caterpillar of a moth, which it becomes as an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: The furry caterpillar called a woolly bear grows up into this garden insect.

clue.text: Rugby player's sneaky little drink

parts.note: fly is British slang for crafty or sneaky
a half is a half-pint of beer, a small drink

explanation.surface: A rugby player has a crafty small drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the fly-half, or stand-off, is a back who directs play.

clue.text: Men network at party in US resort

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
LAN is a local area network
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Men networking at a party in an American holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando in Florida is a major American holiday destination, home to theme parks.

clue.text: Cod with unpleasant smell circling round one's washing

parts.note: cod as an adjective means fake or mock, a sham

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the smell surrounds the other letters

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
a round shape is the letter O
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A smelly fish gets a thorough scrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cod' looks like the fish but is the adjective meaning fake. 'circling' puts O and I inside PONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning hair or a carpet with a soapy lather is a kind of washing.

clue.text: Not the white team, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a team of oxen is a yoke, a pair harnessed together

explanation.surface: A sports side that does not play in white kit, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg has two parts, the white and the yellow centre, so the part that is not the white is that centre.

clue.text: Too trendy to win round barristers, in general

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: round means going around, so these letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: to gain is to win
the Bar is barristers collectively

explanation.surface: Something far too fashionable to persuade the legal profession at large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' sends the win piece around the barristers. 'Too' opens the clue as the whole definition; the Bar means barristers as a body.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as well or in addition, the same as also.

clue.text: Play set in a Southern English town

indicators.note: to play with something is to toy with it and move it about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drama staged in a town in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a drama but rearranges SETINA to STAINE. STAINES is a town in Surrey, near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines-upon-Thames is a town in Surrey, south-west of London.

clue.text: Potential miss — not entirely upset when it's enregistered

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
not entirely says only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A near miss, partly reversed when it gets recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'not entirely' as part of the definition, but it is the indicator that the answer is hidden in the next words; the definition is just 'Potential miss'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is an unmarried girl, and Ernestine is a girl's name she could bear.

clue.text: Idiotic of doctor cutting French department back

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in reverse
cutting means slicing into, so these letters go inside the department

parts.note: Lot is a department in south-west France
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A foolish move by a doctor slashing a French department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' gives LOOFMOT, which 'back' turns round; 'of' is fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, this old word means foolish or silly.

clue.text: Composer not keen on a pop screening please note

parts.note: off means put off or not keen

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the note goes inside

parts.note: a pop means apiece, each
NB is nota bene, please note

explanation.surface: A musician who dislikes pop music, with a note about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pop' is the informal 'each', as in five pounds a pop.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach was a German-born French composer of operettas.

clue.text: Going on pig's back, following ox with family

indicators.note: following places the pig's letter after the ox and family

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox
kin means family

indicators.note: back picks out the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Riding on the back of a pig after an ox, with the whole family.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to talk at length, chattering or nattering.

clue.text: Papa with family forms to fill out

indicators.note: forms means shapes into something new, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A father and his family have paperwork to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forms' looks like paperwork, but signals rearranging P and FAMILY.
explanation.definitionFit: To amplify an account is to enlarge on it, adding detail.

clue.text: Reinforced building before attack: a healthy practice

parts.note: a keep is the strong central tower of a castle
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: A fortified tower before a siege is a sound idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise to stay in shape is a healthy routine.

clue.text: It follows return of airmen to this point

parts.note: thus means therefore, it follows

indicators.note: return of means the airmen's letters are read backwards

parts.note: RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: The airmen's homecoming leads to this place.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up till now or as far as this, so far.

clue.text: Russian leader's wife volunteers to hide chemical weapon

indicators.note: to hide means to hold out of sight inside

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
sarin is a nerve gas

explanation.surface: A Russian first lady hides a nerve agent among volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: The consort of a tsar, the old Russian ruler, was an empress with this title.

clue.text: A lot to bear with difficulty from Cockney youth

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop their aitches

parts.note: to hump is to carry something heavy with effort
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A cockney youth struggles to carry a large load.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means very many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Woman's brought up slippers for repairs in cobbler's?

indicators.note: in a down light brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: her means belonging to a woman
eels are slippery creatures, slippers

explanation.surface: A woman has carried her slippers to the cobbler's for mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippers' looks like footwear but means slippery things, eels.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoemaker fixes worn shoes by fitting new heels to them.

clue.text: Content in the style of old magazine?

definitions.text: Content in the style of old magazine?

parts.words: Content in the style of old magazine?
parts.note: content means happy, and Punch was a long-running British humorous magazine, so happy in Punch's way

explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a British satirical weekly from 1841 to 2002; the idiom comes from the delighted Mr Punch of the puppet shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means highly delighted, so a very content or gratified person.

clue.text: Demanding head should not be involved in quarrel

indicators.note: says the first letter of the word must be dropped

parts.note: stiff means hard or demanding, as a stiff test

explanation.surface: A bossy leader ought to keep out of the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a small squabble, a minor quarrel.

clue.text: Shortest section of the track Nine Ladies Dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nine women dance on the shortest part of an athletics track, echoing the carol's nine ladies dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: On an oval running track the innermost lane is the shortest way round.

clue.text: Girl recalled attempt to chop wood

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the result is read backwards
to chop is to cut into, so the attempt goes inside the wood

parts.note: elm is a kind of wood
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A woman remembered trying to chop timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to chop' puts TRY into ELM giving ELTRYM; 'recalled' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Craft displayed by heads of European Science Institutes

definitions.meaning: small motor boats, a sort of vessel

definitions.text: displayed by heads of European Science Institutes
definitions.meaning: new projects introduced to the public with fanfare by institute directors

explanation.surface: A skill showcased by the directors of European research centres.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both motorboats and public unveilings of new products or projects.
